subject: Canary routing exception request — EU finance account (force EU model, no-fallback)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Julien Dupont <julien.dupont@eurobank.fr>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Canary routing exception request — EuroBank EU finance account

Team —

Quick ask from the EuroBank pilot: they want the initial canary (10% of traffic) to be pinned to an EU-only model variant and to disable automatic fallback to lower-cost variants or other regions for the duration of the canary. Reasoning: procurement and security want absolute data residency guarantees during the pilot and they want to run our new fine-tuned EU model (eu-fin-v1) without any cross-region or auto-fallback behavior.

What I'm requesting: a short-lived routing exception that forces EU region routing and disables the fallback policy for traffic tagged with account_id=DB-12987 and canary=true. Duration requested: 72 hours (with metrics-based extension).

Questions for ops/product/legal:
- Is there a safe, auditable way to enforce no-fallback for a scoped canary?
- What rollback/mitigation guardrails do we need if latency or errors spike?
- Any compliance or contractual concerns (Laur a) for a region-lock request like this?

I've attached the EuroBank canary plan and a checklist. Julien — they want to start next Monday; can you confirm exact start window and constraints?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: eurobank_canary_plan_v2.pdf (PDF)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Julien Dupont <julien.dupont@eurobank.fr>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Canary routing exception request — EuroBank EU finance account

Thanks Aditya — flagged a few immediate concerns. Short answers first: yes, we can implement scoped routing overrides; no-fallback is higher risk but feasible with guardrails.

A few clarifications before I can sign off on an exception:
- Exact metric gates for extension: what KPIs should we watch (p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta)?
- Who is the escalation owner during the 72h window (we need a single point of contact for rollbacks)?
- Does the canary need any change to KV caching or prefix caching that might cause cache misses across regions?

Karthik/Laura/Monica — please reply by end of day with recommended metric thresholds and a rollback playbook snippet. Julien, if procurement insists on EU-only routing, confirm the absolute start date/time and that they accept a measured canary (10%).

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Julien Dupont <julien.dupont@eurobank.fr>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:18:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Canary routing exception request — EuroBank EU finance account

Quick input from GTM: procurement is firm about EU-only for this pilot, and Julien confirmed they will not accept cross-region routing for pilot traffic. Recommended KPIs to gate extension:
- p95 latency <= 450ms (end-to-end)
- error rate < 0.5% (5xx + model timeouts)
- token cost variance < +20% vs baseline

Escalation owner: Aditya will be primary; Hannah to authorize rollback. Rollback trigger: sustained violations for 15 minutes or any material SLA breach affecting live customers.

I can surface this to sales leadership if we need executive-level sign-off, but I think product/ops can handle the technical exception.

—Karthik
From: Julien Dupont <julien.dupont@eurobank.fr>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Canary routing exception request — EuroBank EU finance account

Thanks for the fast responses. EuroBank can start the canary window on Monday 25 May at 08:00 CET. They accept a 10% canary and the metrics thresholds listed by Karthik look reasonable. Procurement requires an auditable trail that shows routing/decisioning for every request in the canary — is that available? Also confirm the longest rollback window (how quickly can you revert routing to global fallback)?

Julien Dupont
Head of Platform Security, EuroBank
procurement@eurobank.fr

On Fri, 22 May 2026 at 11:18, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick input from GTM: procurement is firm about EU-only for this pilot...
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Julien Dupont <julien.dupont@eurobank.fr>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 16:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Canary routing exception request — EuroBank EU finance account

Decision and conditions — approved (temporary exception). Summary below and attached playbooks.

What we're approving:
- Scoped routing override: all traffic with account_id=DB-12987 and canary=true will be routed to the EU-only cluster and forced to model eu-fin-v1 for the initial 72-hour canary window. No automatic fallback to other regions or cheaper model variants while the override is active.

Conditions (must be met before start):
1) Audit trace: enable request-level routing logs to S3 for the canary; provide EuroBank with a read-only link to the log artifacts. (Ops action: Monica)
2) Metric gates: p95 latency <= 450ms, error rate < 0.5%, token cost delta < +20% (as agreed). Continuous monitoring and automated alerting to on-call.
3) Escalation/rollback: Aditya is primary owner; Hannah will trigger rollback. Rollback window: we can revert routing within 3 minutes of an authorized rollback decision; automated rollback if error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m.
4) Cache considerations: prefix/KV caching may result in higher cold-cache latency — product to add a warmup step in the attached checklist. (Product action: Laura)
5) Legal sign-off: procurement accepts for pilot; contract amendment not required for a temporary canary but we will record exception in contract notes. (Legal: Laura)

Start window confirmed by Julien: Monday 25 May 08:00 CET. Aditya — please coordinate a runbook handoff and ensure the eu-route-exemption-checklist.xlsx is completed. Monica — enable the log delivery and attach access link to the Jira ticket before start.

I'll monitor first 2 hours of the canary and will escalate immediately if any red flags. Final decision on extension will be based on rolling metric windows and a short review meeting 72 hours after start.

Thanks everyone — good precedent for future region-locked canaries.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: eurobank_canary_plan_v2.pdf, eu-route-exemption-checklist.xlsx
